results.title: log sources on this project, and whether auth audit events have their own
results.detail: 9 sources in the last 3 h: postgrest_logs, auth_logs, postgres_logs, supavisor_logs, pgbouncer_logs, edge_logs, realtime_logs, storage_logs, auth_audit_logs. auth_audit_logs is present.

results.title: auth events reach auth.audit_log_entries, and which actions GoTrue records
results.detail: 3/3 users created, 3 password logins. 6 rows in auth.audit_log_entries carry the run tag (first row 0s after the writes): login x3, user_signedup x3. The in-database copy is ENABLED on this project.

results.title: the same auth events in the auth_audit_logs source
results.detail: found 6 matching rows in auth_audit_logs, first visible 33s after the writes. This copy is written by the platform, not by the tenant's database, and no tenant credential has a write path to it.

results.title: a forged entry: in the table, not in the stream
results.detail: forged insert -> true; the table now holds 1 row for that actor; the stream holds none after 126s, so the stream is fed by the Auth server and not by the table. A row in one store with no counterpart in the other is the signature - in both directions.

results.title: delete the in-database copy; count both stores again
results.detail: DELETE -> true. Table rows for the tag: 6 before, 0 after. Stream rows for the same tag: 6 before, 6 after. The erasure is complete in the store the tenant owns and invisible in the store the platform owns, so comparing the two counts for one window detects it.

results.title: cleanup
results.detail: 3 auth users deleted; tagged audit rows already removed by A05e

results.title: a fresh auth event through GET /auth/v1/admin/audit
results.detail: user create -> HTTP 200, password login -> HTTP 200. GET /auth/v1/admin/audit (service key) -> HTTP 200, 5 entries, 2 carrying this run's tag (visible 0s after the write). The same event has 2 rows in auth.audit_log_entries (in-database copy enabled).

results.title: the same read after the table rows are deleted
results.detail: DELETE -> true; table rows for the tag 2 -> 0. Endpoint entries carrying the tag: 2 -> 0. The endpoint reads the table: erasing the rows blinds the admin API too, so it is a window rather than a second copy.

results.title: write and delete routes on the admin audit endpoint
results.detail: DELETE /auth/v1/admin/audit -> HTTP 405 (); POST -> HTTP 405 (). A service-key holder has no API path to the audit trail's contents; the database password is the path.

results.title: install a chained mirror fed by a trigger on the audit table
results.detail: schema, chained table, SECURITY DEFINER capture function, verifier and trigger created; 1 trigger now on auth.audit_log_entries. A tenant CAN attach a trigger to the Auth server's own table - the ACL grants postgres the TRIGGER privilege.

results.title: a real auth event reaches the mirror through the trigger
results.detail: admin user create -> HTTP 200, password login -> HTTP 200; the mirror captured the tagged entry 0s later. Mirror holds 2 rows (seq 1..2); verifier: 2 rows checked, first break none. GoTrue writes as supabase_auth_admin and the SECURITY DEFINER function still records it.

results.title: delete one mirror row: does the verifier notice
results.detail: deleted mirror seq 2; verifier now reports first break at seq none over 1 rows. A row removed from the middle of a chain cannot be removed quietly - the next row's prev_hash no longer recomputes.

results.title: the same identity rebuilds the chain and the verifier goes quiet
results.detail: rehash of every row -> true; verifier now reports first break none over 1 rows. The head hash moved from ec83cf53fde2... to ec83cf53fde2..., so the ONE thing that survives an owner with a rehash loop is a head hash that was copied out of the database before the tampering. In-database immutability against the database owner does not exist; off-box anchoring is the control.

results.detail: trigger and schema dropped (0 user triggers left on the audit table); test user deleted
